notes: a(n) = A083143(n)/prime(n); zero iff A083143(n) = 0. For p = prime(n), d = ord_p(10): if d <= n/2, R_d 0^(n-2d) R_d works; else the pair values u_i = 10^i + 10^(n-1-i), 1 <= i <= floor((n-2)/2), take >= ceil(h/2) distinct residues, and Dias da Silva-Hamidoune gives a subset summing to -(10^(n-1)+1), i.e. an n-digit 0/1 palindrome divisible by p, once ceil(h/2) >= floor(sqrt(4p-7))+1, true for all n >= 460 (checked to 20000 with actual primes, analytic beyond). pal.py finds a(n) != 0 for all n <= 460 (18 listed terms agree). Outside Lean: Dias da Silva-Hamidoune theorem, Rosser-Schoenfeld bound, the computations (pal.py, thresh.py).
